01
The Club

A wee club with
a big fighting heart.

Doonhamers is Dumfries' community amateur boxing club — a place where kids, teenagers and adults learn to box properly, build confidence and belong to something.

Coaching is key

Now training from a bigger home at 250 Lochside Road, the club moved into its expanded Lochside gym in January 2026 — with room for more juniors, more sessions and more champions.

Doonhamers boxers compete across Scotland. The club's Alishia Armstrong became the first female Youth Western District titleholder from Dumfries & Galloway, and was picked for Boxing Scotland's Next Generation Group — and even Floyd Mayweather Sr has travelled to Dumfries to coach at the club.

The club also hosts the Robert Burns Box Cup in Dumfries, bringing amateur boxing clubs from across the UK to the town.

03
Head Coach

Coaching is key.

Anne Armstrong
Head Coach — Doonhamers ABC

Anne Armstrong leads Doonhamers with a simple belief: coaching is key. Every boxer — from a five-year-old on their first night to a title-winning youth — gets the same attention, the same standards and the same belief.

Under her coaching, Doonhamers boxers have won Scottish titles, been picked for Boxing Scotland's national pathway, and the club has been recognised with the Unsung Sport Hero Group Award 2026.

Anne also drives the club's charity work through the Armstrong Angel Foundation, supporting the Dumfries community beyond the ring.

Ask Coach Anne a question →

“There's nothing more powerful than a humble person with a warrior spirit.”
